name: Meteosat pictures (clouds and dust)
summary: Two pictures of the eastern Mediterranean from the Meteosat weather satellites, fetched about every hour: clouds in natural colours, and a dust map. Pictures, not numbers.

el.name: Εικόνες Meteosat (σύννεφα και σκόνη)
el.summary: Δύο εικόνες της ανατολικής Μεσογείου από τους μετεωρολογικούς δορυφόρους Meteosat, περίπου κάθε ώρα: σύννεφα με φυσικά χρώματα και ένας χάρτης σκόνης. Είναι εικόνες, όχι αριθμοί.

restrictions: Only RGB image products are used: the EUMETSAT data policy calls them core data, free under CC BY 4.0
The credit line carries the year the picture was made; coastlines and borders are credited to Natural Earth
EUMETView is busy at times and queues requests, so we ask for one picture at a time

update.note: New frames every 10 to 15 minutes; we fetch about every 45 minutes

quality.uncertainty: Pictures, not measurements. One pixel is about 1 to 5 km wide over Cyprus, and thick cloud hides what is below it.
known_issues: Meteosat looks at Cyprus at a slant, so details are coarser than in a picture from a polar satellite
Low clouds and thin or low dust over the sea are hard to see in the dust map
The night version of the cloud picture is drawn from infrared (heat) data and is not a photo
When the server cannot tell us the exact time of the newest frame, the time shown is approximate

upstream.name: EUMETSAT Meteosat (MTG-I1 / Meteosat-12 and MSG) image products

use_for: Showing where clouds and fronts are over the region
Seeing a Saharan dust plume come towards Cyprus
not_for: Rain or cloud amounts at one school
Dust amounts in micrograms: use the air-quality model for that

notes: Layer names are from EUMETSAT-related pages and public code, not from the live service (not reachable from the sandbox); mtg_fd:rgb_geocolour and msg_iodc:rgb_dust are the first choices and each has a fallback. The licence was read in the EUMETSAT data policy (last amended 25 Nov 2025), not in the WMS capabilities.
